Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- The patient primarily presents with soreness and cracked skin on the hands, aggravated by occupational exposure to cleaning products without glove protection. Symptoms align with Contact Dermatitis, particularly given the job change and use of cleaning agents.
- Assessment considers Contact Dermatitis as highly likely, consistent with both transcript and DDx.

Management Plan
- Management includes wearing gloves to avoid exposure to cleaning products, use of steroid creams for inflammation, and stronger emollients applied 3-4 times daily. Follow-up recommended if no improvement in two weeks.

- Allergic Contact Dermatitis: Low likelihood, due to the absence of known allergens and antihistamine inefficacy.
